evals.prompt: I'm building a Telegram Mini App for my e-commerce bot. I need a basic HTML page that shows the user's name from Telegram, has a 'Checkout' button at the bottom that uses Telegram's native button, and when clicked it sends the cart data back to my bot. The cart is just [{id: 1, name: 'Widget', qty: 2}]. Can you build this?
evals.expected_output: A complete HTML file that: includes the telegram-web-app.js SDK script first, calls tg.ready() and optionally tg.expand(), reads the user name from tg.initDataUnsafe.user, sets up tg.MainButton with text 'Checkout', uses tg.sendData() or an HTTP call to send cart data, and applies at least one CSS variable for theming.

assertions.name: SDK script included before other JS
assertions.description: The telegram-web-app.js script tag appears in the HTML head before any custom JavaScript

assertions.name: ready() called
assertions.description: tg.ready() is called to signal the app is ready to display

assertions.name: Uses MainButton not a plain HTML button for checkout
assertions.description: Uses tg.MainButton to show the checkout CTA, not just a raw HTML button

assertions.name: Sends cart data to bot
assertions.description: Uses tg.sendData() or HTTP fetch with initData auth to deliver cart data

assertions.name: Theme CSS variables used
assertions.description: At least one --tg-theme-* CSS variable is referenced for theming

assertions.name: User name displayed from initDataUnsafe
assertions.description: Reads tg.initDataUnsafe.user.first_name or similar for display

evals.prompt: I have a Telegram Mini App where users submit forms. I need Node.js/Express backend code that validates the initData coming from the Mini App (sent in the Authorization header as 'tma <initData>') and rejects invalid or expired requests. My bot token is in process.env.BOT_TOKEN.
evals.expected_output: Node.js code that: extracts initData from the Authorization header, parses the URL-encoded string, removes 'hash', sorts remaining fields alphabetically, builds the check string with newlines, computes HMAC-SHA256 using 'WebAppData' as the HMAC key for the bot token, then HMAC again with the secret key, uses constant-time comparison, checks auth_date recency.

assertions.name: Uses HMAC-SHA256 with WebAppData key
assertions.description: Creates secretKey using HMAC-SHA256('WebAppData', botToken)

assertions.name: Sorts fields alphabetically
assertions.description: Sorts the key=value pairs alphabetically before building the check string

assertions.name: Excludes hash from check string
assertions.description: Removes the 'hash' field before building the data check string

assertions.name: Uses constant-time comparison
assertions.description: Uses crypto.timingSafeEqual or equivalent, not === for hash comparison

assertions.name: Checks auth_date freshness
assertions.description: Verifies auth_date is recent (within some time window like 3600s)

assertions.name: Returns 401 on invalid
assertions.description: Returns HTTP 401 when validation fails

evals.prompt: I'm creating a Telegram Mini App that looks native — it should adapt to dark/light mode automatically, show a back button when navigating to sub-pages, give haptic feedback when items are selected, and respect the device safe areas (notch/home bar). Show me how to implement all of this.
evals.expected_output: Code showing: CSS variables --tg-theme-* for colors, tg.onEvent('themeChanged',...) handler, tg.BackButton.show/hide for navigation, tg.HapticFeedback usage (impactOccurred and/or selectionChanged), safe area CSS with --tg-safe-area-inset-* variables, and optionally viewportStableHeight usage.

assertions.name: CSS theme variables used for adaptive colors
assertions.description: Uses var(--tg-theme-bg-color) and similar for automatic dark/light adaptation

assertions.name: themeChanged event handled
assertions.description: Listens to tg.onEvent('themeChanged', ...) to update dynamic styles

assertions.name: BackButton controlled for navigation
assertions.description: Shows tg.BackButton when on sub-pages and hides on root

assertions.name: HapticFeedback used
assertions.description: Calls tg.HapticFeedback.impactOccurred() or selectionChanged() for tactile response

assertions.name: Safe area insets respected
assertions.description: Uses --tg-safe-area-inset-bottom or --tg-content-safe-area-inset-* CSS vars

evals.prompt: I'm building a multi-page Telegram Mini App (product list → product detail → checkout). Each sub-page should show the Telegram back button, and tapping it should go back one level. I also want page transitions (slide in from right). Walk me through the navigation implementation.
evals.expected_output: Code that: uses a single BackButton handler pattern with offClick before onClick (to prevent handler stacking), shows BackButton on sub-pages and hides on root, navigates between named div-based pages or uses a hash router, ideally includes CSS page transition animations. Must not call onClick multiple times without offClick.

assertions.name: offClick called before re-registering BackButton handler
assertions.description: The implementation removes the previous handler with offClick before calling onClick, preventing handler stacking

assertions.name: BackButton hidden on root page
assertions.description: BackButton.hide() is called when navigating back to the root/home page

assertions.name: BackButton shown on sub-pages
assertions.description: BackButton.show() is called when pushing to a sub-page

assertions.name: No location.href or page reloads for navigation
assertions.description: Navigation uses div show/hide, hash changes, or framework router — not full page loads

assertions.name: Three distinct pages implemented
assertions.description: At least three page states (list, detail, checkout) are represented

evals.prompt: I want to add Telegram Stars payment to my Mini App. Users should be able to buy 'Premium Access' for 100 Stars. Walk me through the complete flow — frontend JS, backend invoice creation (Python/FastAPI), and the bot handlers for pre_checkout_query and successful_payment.
evals.expected_output: A complete Stars payment implementation including: backend create_invoice_link call with currency='XTR', frontend openInvoice() call with status callback, bot handler for pre_checkout_query that answers within 10s, bot handler for successful_payment that saves the charge_id and activates the purchase. Should note that 'paid' status in openInvoice callback is not authoritative.

assertions.name: Currency set to XTR
assertions.description: Invoice is created with currency='XTR' (Telegram Stars), not USD or other fiat

assertions.name: openInvoice used on frontend
assertions.description: Uses tg.openInvoice(url, callback) to show the payment sheet

assertions.name: pre_checkout_query answered within deadline
assertions.description: pre_checkout_query handler answers within 10 seconds; code shows timeout awareness (asyncio.wait_for, timeout param, or explicit note)

assertions.name: successful_payment handler saves charge_id
assertions.description: Saves telegram_payment_charge_id from the successful_payment message for refund capability

assertions.name: paid callback status noted as non-authoritative
assertions.description: Code or comment indicates that 'paid' in the openInvoice callback must be verified server-side via successful_payment update

evals.prompt: I'm starting a new Telegram Mini App project and want to develop it locally in a browser without opening Telegram every time I make a change. How do I set up local development? I'm using plain HTML/JS.
evals.expected_output: Instructions that include: the miniapp-mock.js file (or equivalent polyfill) added as the first script before the Telegram SDK, explanation that it activates in browser when tgWebAppData is absent, mention of HTTPS requirement for actual Telegram testing and how to solve it (ngrok or similar tunnel), and ideally that window.isTelegramMockActive is set so app code can detect the mock.

assertions.name: Mock script loaded before Telegram SDK
assertions.description: The mock/polyfill script appears before telegram-web-app.js in the HTML — loading order is explicit

assertions.name: Mock activates only in browser, not inside Telegram
assertions.description: Explains or implements the detection: mock is inactive when tgWebAppData param is present (i.e., inside Telegram)

assertions.name: HTTPS requirement for Telegram mentioned
assertions.description: Notes that actual Telegram testing requires HTTPS and suggests ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, or similar

assertions.name: Core API stubs functional in browser
assertions.description: The mock or instructions ensure tg.MainButton, tg.initDataUnsafe.user, tg.ready(), and tg.expand() work in a plain browser
